Method of Attack: Blocks security vendor certificates by adding them to the Windows registry key HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\SystemCertificates\Disallowed\Certificates, preventing signed security programs from running
Modifies Windows HOSTS file to redirect Avast.com hostnames to 127.0.0.1, blocking Avast security program connectivity
Discoverer: Jérôme.B (ToolsLib.com co-administrator and Malwarebytes AdwCleaner developer)
Impacted Systems: Security programs signed by blocked certificates including ESET, Malwarebytes, Avast, AVG, Adaware, Avira, BitDefender, BullGuard, Checkpoint Software, Comodo, CurioLab, Doctor Web, Emsisoft, F-Secure, FRISK, GData, K7 Computing, Kaspersky, McAfee, PC Tools, Panda, SUPERAntiSpyware, Safer Networking, Symantec, ThreatTrack Security, Total Defense, Trend Micro, Webroot
Attack Vector: Installation via unwanted program bundles such as miners
Modification of Windows registry and HOSTS file
Indicators of Compromise: Registry keys under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\SystemCertificates\Disallowed\Certificates\ with certificate thumbprints (e.g. F83099622B4A9F72CB5081F742164AD1B8D048C9 for ESET)
Modified Windows HOSTS file entries redirecting Avast.com hostnames to 127.0.0.1
